rows.onset_pattern: Gradual — physical antenna degradation typically builds progressively due to hardware wear, moisture ingress, or connector corrosion, rather than switching instantaneously.
rows.3gpp_reference: TS 38.141-1 §4.2.1 (BS type 1-C conducted requirement reference points; antenna connector) + TS 38.141-1 §7.2 (Reference sensitivity level)
rows.clause_text: §4.2.1 (BS type 1-C): requirements apply at the BS antenna connector (port A); if an external amplifier or filter is used, requirements apply at the far-end antenna connector (port B). §7.2.1 (Reference sensitivity level): PREFSENS is the minimum mean power received at the antenna connector at which a throughput requirement shall be met for a specified reference measurement channel. (Paraphrased from Rel-19 V19.3.0.)
rows.causal_mechanism: Physical antenna degradation or disconnection reduces the effective radiated power and received signal sensitivity at the O-RU. RSRP drops as the reference signal received from the gNB weakens. UL_SNR collapses because the uplink receive chain is impaired. BLER rises as the link quality falls below the threshold for reliable block decoding. MCS is forced downward by the AMC algorithm responding to the degraded BLER. Distinguished from Co-Channel Interference by the absence of inter-cell signal patterns and by simultaneous degradation across both UL and DL chains.
rows.oran_component_rationale: Antenna functions, RF transmission, and receiver chains are physically located at the O-RU. Antenna failure is a hardware fault at the radio unit layer.
rows.kg_evidence_summary: KG contains AAS BS, antenna array, composite antenna, receiver RF requirements, transmitter characteristics, and OTA co-location requirements from TS 38.141-1 and TS 38.104. TS 38.141-1 §4.2.1 explicitly defines the BS antenna connector reference point and shows external TX/RX filter paths.
rows.notes: Upgraded from §4 (too broad) to §4.2.1 + §7.2 (specific subclauses confirmed in Rel-19 V19.3.0). These clauses provide mechanism-level RF evidence rather than an explicit 'antenna failure' fault definition. v1.3: clause_text quote from v1.2 was not verbatim spec text; replaced.

rows.onset_pattern: Gradual — buffer saturation builds over time as incoming data rate persistently exceeds allocated uplink capacity; does not switch instantaneously.
rows.3gpp_reference: TS 38.321 §6.1.3.1 (Buffer Status Report MAC CEs — Short BSR, Long BSR, Extended BSR, Truncated BSR formats) + TS 38.321 §5.4.5 (Buffer Status Reporting procedure — when and how the UE reports buffer status to the gNB)
rows.clause_text: §6.1.3.1 defines the Buffer Status Report MAC Control Elements (formats named in §5.4.5 include Short, Long, Refined Long, Short/Long Truncated and Extended Short/Long BSR). §5.4.5 defines the BSR procedure: it informs the serving gNB about UL data volume in the MAC entity; BSRs are triggered as Regular, Padding or Periodic and controlled by periodicBSR-Timer, retxBSR-Timer and logicalChannelSR-DelayTimer; a Regular BSR with no suitable UL grant triggers a Scheduling Request (§5.4.4). (Paraphrased from Rel-19.)
rows.causal_mechanism: The MAC scheduler at the O-DU allocates uplink PRBs based on Buffer Status Reports (BSRs) sent by the UE. When incoming data rate persistently exceeds the allocated uplink capacity, the UE uplink buffer (Estimated_UL_Buffer) grows without bound. As the buffer saturates, queuing delay increases, triggering retransmissions (rising UL_BLER) and reducing effective throughput (TX_Bytes). The BSR MAC control element signals buffer occupancy to the gNB, but if the scheduler cannot allocate sufficient PRBs, the buffer overflows. Distinguished from High Network Congestion by the focus on UE-side buffer saturation rather than cell-wide PRB exhaustion. Important: BSR signals buffer status but does not define 'buffer overflow' as a fault; the causal mapping is therefore mechanism-level.
rows.oran_component_rationale: The MAC scheduler responsible for uplink PRB allocation and BSR processing runs in the O-DU. Buffer overflow is a scheduling/resource allocation failure at the O-DU layer.
rows.kg_evidence_summary: KG contains Buffer Status Report as a MAC control element, periodicBSR-Timer, retxBSR-Timer, MAC-CellGroupConfig, RLC buffer Payload, and soft buffer from TS 38.321 and TS 38.523.
rows.notes: REFERENCE CORRECTION (v1.0→v1.2): §5.4 was wrong — §5.4 in TS 38.321 is 'UL-SCH data transfer', not the BSR procedure. Corrected to §5.4.5 (Buffer Status Reporting procedure). §6.1.3.1 confirmed: defines BSR MAC CE formats. Support class retained at Mechanism-level: BSR signals buffer occupancy but does not define buffer overflow as a fault. v1.3: leftover '§5.4 defines the BSR procedure' in clause_text fixed.

rows.onset_pattern: Instantaneous — interference from a neighboring cell is present or absent; onset is not gradual. The mild/severe distinction reflects interference power level, not onset speed.
rows.3gpp_reference: TS 38.141-1 §7.8 (In-channel selectivity — receiver tolerance to a stronger time-aligned in-channel NR interferer; conformance test)
rows.clause_text: §7.8.1 In-channel selectivity: the receiver's ability to receive a wanted signal at its assigned resource blocks in the presence of an interfering signal received at a larger power spectral density, with a throughput requirement on a specified reference measurement channel; the interferer is an NR signal time-aligned with the wanted signal. The clause does not describe a neighbour-cell or co-channel-from-another-cell scenario. (Paraphrased from Rel-19.) Subsections: definition and applicability, minimum requirement, test purpose, method of test, test requirements.
rows.causal_mechanism: Co-channel interference occurs when a neighboring cell transmits on the same or overlapping frequency resources, causing UL_SNR to degrade at the gNB receiver. In the mild case, UL_SNR declines moderately but does not collapse. UL_BLER rises as decoding errors increase. PRB utilization remains stable — this stability distinguishes mild CCI from congestion, where PRB utilization would be elevated. DL_MCS may drop slightly as the AMC algorithm responds to worsened link quality.
rows.oran_component_rationale: Co-channel interference is a physical-layer RF phenomenon occurring at the receive chain of the O-RU.
rows.kg_evidence_summary: KG contains in-device coexistence interference, IDC assistance information, in-channel selectivity, co-location blocking, guardband, minimum guardband, SINR-related measurements, and Zero Forcing from TS 38.141-1 and TS 38.104.
rows.notes: SUPPORT CLASS DOWNGRADED (Directly supportable → Mechanism-level) in v1.2 and CONFIRMED in v1.3: §7.8.1 defines in-channel selectivity as tolerance to a stronger, time-aligned NR interferer within the channel (a conformance test), not neighbour-cell co-channel interference as in TelecomTS. The degradation mechanism is analogous but the test scenario differs. v1.3: clause_text and 3gpp_reference wording ('co-channel interfering signal') corrected to match the spec; pending check on §7.8.1 closed.

rows.onset_pattern: Instantaneous — same as Mild CCI. Severity reflects interference power level at injection time, not a different temporal onset mechanism.
rows.3gpp_reference: TS 38.141-1 §7.8 (In-channel selectivity) + TS 38.104 §4.9 (OTA co-location with other base stations; requirements ensuring co-located systems operate with minimal mutual degradation)
rows.clause_text: §7.8: same as Mild CCI row (time-aligned in-channel NR interferer at larger PSD; no neighbour-cell scenario). TS 38.104 §4.9: co-location requirements assume a BS type 1-O co-located with another BS of the same class so that both can operate with minimal degradation to each other; unwanted-emission and out-of-band-blocking co-location requirements are optional by declaration, TX OFF and TX IMD are mandatory. This is an OTA, co-sited requirement, not neighbour-cell interference, so it is secondary evidence only. (Paraphrased from Rel-19.)
rows.causal_mechanism: In severe co-channel interference, the interfering neighbor signal is strong enough to cause UL_SNR to collapse significantly below the threshold for reliable decoding. UL_BLER rises sharply and DL_MCS is forced to its minimum values. RSRP may remain nominally acceptable but the interference-to-signal ratio overwhelms the receiver. Unlike mild CCI, severe CCI may cause connectivity loss. PRB_Utilization remains stable — elevated PRB utilization would shift the diagnosis toward congestion. The severity distinction comes from TelecomTS anomaly injection parameters, not from 3GPP.
rows.oran_component_rationale: Severe CCI remains a physical-layer RF phenomenon at the O-RU receive chain. The Near-RT RIC may be involved in interference mitigation response via xApp, but the primary component experiencing the fault is the O-RU.
rows.oran_spec_reference: O-RAN.WG4.MP; O-RAN.WG3.E2 (Near-RT RIC E2 interface for interference management xApp response)
rows.kg_evidence_summary: Same KG evidence as Mild CCI plus TX IMD co-location requirements and out-of-band blocking co-location requirements from TS 38.104 §4.9.
rows.notes: SUPPORT CLASS DOWNGRADED (Directly supportable → Mechanism-level) in v1.2 and CONFIRMED in v1.3. Same caveat as CCI Mild. TS 38.104 §4.9 applies to BS type 1-O co-located with another BS of the same class (0.1 m reference antenna separation), so it is weak support for neighbour-cell interference; keep as secondary evidence or drop. Pending check on §7.8.1 closed.

rows.onset_pattern: Gradual — channel aging worsens continuously with increasing UE velocity; degradation accumulates over time rather than appearing instantaneously.
rows.3gpp_reference: TR 38.901 §7.6.6 (Time-varying Doppler shift — defines Doppler as derivative of channel phase over time as a function of UE velocity vector v(t)) + TR 38.901 §7.6.10 (Dual mobility — extends Doppler to simultaneous Tx and Rx mobility; Doppler frequency v_n,m = (r_hat_rx,n,m · v_rx + r_hat_tx,n,m · v_tx) / lambda_0 for LOS paths)
rows.clause_text: TR 38.901 §7.6.6 (Time-varying Doppler shift): 'The Doppler shift generally depends on the time evolution of the channel as it is defined as the derivative of the channel phase over time. It can be the result from Tx, Rx, or scatterer movement.' The general exponential Doppler term (Equation 7.6-31): exp(j2pi * integral from t0 to t of [r_hat_rx,n,m(t_tilde) · v(t_tilde) / lambda_0] dt_tilde), where r_hat_rx,n,m(t) is the normalized vector pointing into the direction of the incoming wave as seen from the Rx at time t, v(t) is the velocity vector of the Rx at time t, and t0 is a reference point defining the initial phase (t0=0). Note: Equation 7.5-22 holds only for time-invariant Doppler shift where r_hat_rx,n,m(t)·v(t) = r_hat_rx,n,m · v (constant velocity vector). TR 38.901 §7.6.10 (Dual mobility): 'To support simulations that involve dual Tx and Rx mobility or scatterer mobility, the Doppler frequency component in the channel coefficient generation in step 11 in clause 7.5 should be updated as follows. For the LOS path, the Doppler frequency is given by v_n,m = (r_hat_rx,n,m · v_rx + r_hat_tx,n,m · v_tx) / lambda_0. For all other paths, the Doppler frequency component includes an additional scatterer velocity term D_n,m drawn from [-v_scatt, v_scatt] with Bernoulli-distributed mobility parameter p (typical value p=0.2).'
rows.causal_mechanism: At high UE velocity, the time-varying Doppler term (TR 38.901 Eq. 7.6-31) produces rapid channel phase variation proportional to v(t)/lambda_0. When UE speed exceeds the channel estimation coherence time, the gNB scheduler cannot track the channel accurately, forcing conservative MCS selection (DL_MCS reduction) and causing RSRP fluctuation. Dual mobility (§7.6.10) compounds this when scatterers also move (D_n,m term), increasing the effective Doppler spread beyond what a single-velocity model predicts, further degrading UL_NPRB allocation and TX_Bytes throughput.
rows.oran_component_rationale: Doppler shift is a physical propagation phenomenon (O-RU layer) but its primary measurable impact is on MAC scheduling and MCS selection decisions at the O-DU. Both components are involved.
rows.oran_spec_reference: O-RAN.WG4.MP (O-RU physical channel handling); O-RAN.WG6.O2 (O-DU management)
rows.kg_evidence_summary: KG did not establish a literal Doppler entity. TS 38.141-1 Annex G.2 (prior reference) could not be confirmed with sufficient evidence and has been replaced by TR 38.901 §7.6.6 + §7.6.10 pending PDF confirmation.
rows.notes:
CONFIRMED against primary PDF (ETSI TR 138 901 V19.1.0). §7.6.6 confirmed: defines time-varying Doppler as derivative of channel phase over time, Equation 7.6-31 gives the general exponential Doppler term with velocity vector v(t). §7.6.10 confirmed: Dual Mobility extends model to simultaneous Tx+Rx+scatterer movement. clause_text updated with direct quotes from PDF. Document type: TR (Technical Report, informative channel model) — not TS. validate_citation() regex must accept T[SR] prefix to pass for this row.
Legacy validation/evidence note: Primary PDF — ETSI TR 138 901 V19.1.0, Sections 7.6.6 and 7.6.10, Equation 7.6-31

rows.onset_pattern: Gradual — ping-pong oscillation builds as the UE remains in motion between two cells with nearly equal signal strength; does not appear as a single instantaneous event.
rows.3gpp_reference: TS 38.331 §5.5.4.4 (Event A3: neighbour becomes offset better than SpCell — defines measurement event trigger condition with hysteresis and a3-Offset parameters that govern handover initiation thresholds) + TS 38.331 §5.5.4.1 (Measurement report triggering, General — entering/leaving conditions must hold for timeToTrigger)
rows.clause_text: TS 38.331 §5.5.4.4 (Event A3 — Neighbour becomes offset better than SpCell): entering condition A3-1: Mn + Ofn + Ocn - Hys > Mp + Ofp + Ocp + Off; leaving condition A3-2: Mn + Ofn + Ocn + Hys < Mp + Ofp + Ocp + Off. Mn/Mp are the neighbour and SpCell measurement results (dBm for RSRP), Ofn/Ofp the measurement-object offsets, Ocn/Ocp the cell individual offsets, Hys the hysteresis (hysteresis in reportConfigNR) and Off the a3-Offset in reportConfigNR; all offsets in dB. §5.5.4.1 (General): for event-triggered reporting the entering (or leaving) condition must hold for all measurements after layer 3 filtering during timeToTrigger before the UE initiates measurement reporting. Event A3 only triggers a measurement report; the handover decision is made by the network. That too-small a3-Offset, hysteresis or timeToTrigger causes ping-pong handovers is the project's mechanism claim (from the cited literature), not text of the clause. (Formulas and paraphrase from Rel-19.)
rows.causal_mechanism: TS 38.331 §5.5.4.4 defines Event A3 which triggers when a neighbour cell signal exceeds the serving cell by a3-Offset with hysteresis applied (and, per §5.5.4.1, for the duration of timeToTrigger). A faulty handover algorithm misconfigures a3-Offset too small, hysteresis too low, or timeToTrigger too short, causing the UE to oscillate between cells (ping-pong handover). Each unnecessary handover causes a brief service interruption (RSRP oscillation, packet loss spike in UL_NumberOfPackets and UL_BLER), followed by partial recovery — producing the oscillatory KPI pattern observed in TelecomTS.
rows.oran_component_rationale: Handover parameter control (A3 event thresholds, hysteresis, time-to-trigger) may be managed by Near-RT RIC xApps via the E2 interface in O-RAN deployments. The KG contains Near-RT RIC traffic steering, cell reselection/handover parameter adjustment, and E2 control procedures. This is an architectural mapping.
rows.oran_spec_reference: O-RAN.WG3.E2 (E2 interface — Near-RT RIC to E2 Node, handover parameter control); O-RAN.WG2.A1 (A1 interface, RIC policy from Non-RT RIC)
rows.kg_evidence_summary: KG contains HANDOVER REQUIRED, HANDOVER REQUEST, Handover Notify, conditional handover (condHandover-r16), handover failure (condHandoverFailure-r16), Handover Failure Log Reporting, Relative Time Stamp Accuracy, N1-to-N1 handover, X2AP handover procedures, and Dual Active Protocol Stack from TS 38.133, TS 38.523, and TS 32.423. (KG content only; the primary reference for this row is TS 38.331.)
rows.notes: REFERENCE REPLACED (v1.1→v1.2): TS 38.133 §4.3.5 (Relative Timestamp Accuracy) was wrong for this fault — it covers logging accuracy, not handover triggers. Replaced with TS 38.331 §5.5.4.4 (Event A3), confirmed in Rel-19. v1.3: 3gpp_version updated to TS 38.331 V19.4.0, §5.5.4.1 added because timeToTrigger is applied there, clause_text carries A3 inequalities.

rows.onset_pattern: Gradual — RF filter degradation typically worsens progressively due to environmental factors such as moisture ingress and temperature cycling.
rows.3gpp_reference: TS 38.141-1 §7.5 (Out-of-band blocking — receiver performance under out-of-band interference caused by filter degradation) + TS 38.141-1 §7.6 (Receiver spurious emissions) + TS 38.104 §6.6 (Unwanted emissions — transmitter spurious emissions caused by faulty RF filter stopband failure)
rows.clause_text: TS 38.141-1 §7.5.1 (Out-of-band blocking — General): 'The out-of-band blocking characteristic is a measure of the receiver ability to receive a wanted signal at its assigned channel at the antenna connector for BS type 1-C or TAB connector for BS type 1-H in the presence of an unwanted interferer out of the operating band, which is a CW signal for out-of-band blocking.' §7.5.5.1 specifies measurement uncertainty limits for the blocking test across carrier frequency ranges (e.g., fwanted ≤ 3 GHz: interferer level ±1.0 dB up to 3 GHz; system uncertainty = SQRT(wanted_level_error² + interferer_level_error²) + broadband noise effect). TS 38.141-1 §7.6.1 (Receiver spurious emissions — General): 'The receiver spurious emissions power is the power of emissions generated or amplified in a receiver unit that appear at the antenna connector (for BS type 1-C) or at the TAB connector (for BS type 1-H). The requirements apply to all BS with separate RX and TX antenna connectors / TAB connectors.' §7.6.5.2/§7.6.5.3 specifies emission limits: 30 MHz ≤ f ≤ 4 GHz: ±2.0 dB; 4 GHz < f ≤ 19 GHz: ±4.0 dB; 19 GHz < f ≤ 26 GHz: ±4.5 dB. TS 38.104 §7.5.1 (Out-of-band blocking definition, BS type 1-C): same definition as TS 38.141-1 §7.5.1 — confirmed in TS 38.104 V19.2.0.
rows.causal_mechanism: Degraded RF filters at the O-RU allow out-of-band interference to pass through the receiver front-end, raising the effective noise floor and degrading UL_SNR. On the transmit side, a failed filter stopband allows spurious emissions to leak into adjacent bands, causing self-interference and potentially violating regulatory emission limits. The combined effect degrades RSRP and increases UL_BLER. Distinguished from CCI in that faulty RF filters affect all received signals uniformly rather than from a specific directional source.
rows.oran_component_rationale: RF filters are physical components located in the O-RU RF chain. Both the receiver filter and the transmit filter are O-RU hardware components.
rows.oran_spec_reference: O-RAN.WG4.MP (Fronthaul interface, O-RU RF chain management)
rows.kg_evidence_summary: KG contains OTA out-of-band blocking (TS 38.141-1 §7.5), receiver spurious emissions (§7.6), out-of-band blocking co-location requirements (TS 38.104 §4.9), OTA in-channel selectivity, and receiver blocking/selectivity requirements.
rows.notes: CONFIRMED (v1.3 → v1.4): clause_text updated with direct quotes from primary PDFs. §7.5.1 confirmed from TS 38.141-1 V19.3.0: defines out-of-band blocking as receiver ability to handle CW interferer outside operating band. §7.5.5.1 confirms measurement uncertainty table (fwanted ≤ 3 GHz: ±1.3 dB to ±3.2 dB by interferer frequency). §7.6.1 confirmed from TS 38.141-1 V19.3.0: defines receiver spurious emissions as power generated or amplified in receiver appearing at antenna connector. §7.6.5.2/§7.6.5.3 emission limits confirmed numerically. TS 38.104 §7.5.1 confirms same out-of-band blocking definition in V19.2.0. Previous note '(Paraphrased from Rel-19.)' removed — clause_text now contains direct quotes. support_class remains Mechanism-level: these clauses define test requirements for RF filter performance rather than directly specifying 'faulty RF filter' as a fault category.

rows.onset_pattern: Gradual — PRB utilization rises steadily as persistent traffic load accumulates over time; does not switch instantaneously.
rows.3gpp_reference: TS 28.552 §5.1.1.2.1 (DL Total PRB Usage — measurement definition for monitoring DL radio resource utilization) + TS 28.552 §5.1.1.2.2 (UL Total PRB Usage — measurement definition for monitoring UL radio resource utilization)
rows.clause_text: TS 28.552 §5.1.1.2.1 DL Total PRB Usage: the usage, in percentage, of physical resource blocks on the downlink for any purpose, optionally split per PLMN ID, S-NSSAI and QoS resource type; measurement name RRU.PrbDl; measured per NRCellDU; one use is monitoring the load of the radio physical layer. §5.1.1.2.2 UL Total PRB Usage: the corresponding uplink measurement. (Paraphrased; clause titles confirmed in Rel-19 V19.6.0, definition text read on a later-release page.)
rows.causal_mechanism: Gradual buildup high network congestion occurs when traffic demand progressively accumulates over time, steadily driving PRB utilization toward saturation in both uplink and downlink. As PRB utilization increases, scheduling headroom decreases, causing Estimated_UL_Buffer to grow and throughput (TX_Bytes) to plateau while MCS levels degrade. Distinguished from Buffer Overflow by cell-wide PRB saturation rather than single-UE buffer saturation.
rows.oran_component_rationale: The MAC scheduler responsible for PRB allocation runs in the O-DU. Congestion is fundamentally a scheduling resource exhaustion problem at the O-DU layer.
rows.oran_spec_reference: O-RAN.WG6.O2 (O2 interface, O-DU management); O-RAN.WG3.E2 (Near-RT RIC load balancing xApp via E2)
rows.kg_evidence_summary: TS 28.552 Rel-19 V19.6.0 explicitly defines §5.1.1.2.1 as DL Total PRB Usage and §5.1.1.2.2 as UL Total PRB Usage including percentage of PRBs used. This is the strongest measured-by mapping in the table.
rows.notes: ONSET CORRECTED in v1.2 (Instantaneous → Gradual). TS 38.314 §4 REMOVED from reference: it is a cross-reference (§4.2.1.6) to TS 28.552, not an independent definition. Primary governing spec is TS 28.552 §5.1.1.2.1 + §5.1.1.2.2. v1.4: causal_mechanism text updated to match the gradual onset profile.

rows.onset_pattern: Instantaneous — a sudden traffic burst saturates PRB capacity rapidly; PRB utilization rises sharply rather than gradually.
rows.3gpp_reference: TS 28.552 §5.1.1.2.1 (DL Total PRB Usage — measurement definition for monitoring DL radio resource utilization) + TS 28.552 §5.1.1.2.2 (UL Total PRB Usage — measurement definition for monitoring UL radio resource utilization)
rows.clause_text: Same as Row 8 — TS 28.552 §5.1.1.2.1 DL Total PRB Usage (RRU.PrbDl) and §5.1.1.2.2 UL Total PRB Usage from Rel-19 V19.6.0. The temporal/static distinction is in the TelecomTS anomaly injection model, not in the governing specification.
rows.causal_mechanism: Sudden spike high network congestion occurs when an abrupt traffic burst rapidly saturates PRB capacity in both uplink and downlink. PRB utilization surges instantaneously during the burst, causing immediate Estimated_UL_Buffer accumulation, a drop in throughput (TX_Bytes), and MCS degradation. Once the burst subsides, metrics recover. Shares governing specifications (TS 28.552 §5.1.1.2.1 + §5.1.1.2.2) with Gradual Buildup; the key distinction is the abrupt, instantaneous temporal onset profile.
rows.oran_component_rationale: Same as Static Congestion — MAC scheduler at the O-DU is the primary component managing resource allocation under temporal load surges.
rows.oran_spec_reference: O-RAN.WG6.O2 (O2 interface, O-DU management); O-RAN.WG3.E2 (Near-RT RIC load balancing xApp)
rows.kg_evidence_summary: Same KG evidence as Static Congestion. The temporal distinction is in anomaly behavior (TelecomTS injection model), not in the governing 3GPP specification.
rows.notes: ONSET CORRECTED in v1.2 (Gradual → Instantaneous). TS 38.314 §4 REMOVED: same reason as Row 8. Shares governing clause (TS 28.552 §5.1.1.2.1 + §5.1.1.2.2) with Row 8; distinction is in onset pattern and temporal KPI progression. v1.4: causal_mechanism text updated to match the abrupt/instantaneous onset profile.

rows.onset_pattern: Gradual — software bugs often manifest intermittently under specific load conditions or timing interactions, causing erratic PRB allocation patterns that worsen over time rather than appearing as an instantaneous step change.
rows.3gpp_reference: TS 38.321 §5.4.3.1.3 (Allocation of resources — token-bucket LCP resource allocation procedure defining how the MAC entity allocates UL grants across logical channels using Bj token variable and PBR-based priority ordering)
rows.clause_text: TS 38.321 §5.4.3.1.3 (Allocation of resources): 'The MAC entity shall, when a new transmission is performed, allocate resources to the logical channels as follows: logical channels selected in clause 5.4.3.1.2 for the UL grant with Bj > 0 are allocated resources in a decreasing priority order. If the PBR of a logical channel is set to infinity, the MAC entity shall allocate resources for all the data that is available for transmission on the logical channel before meeting the PBR of the lower priority logical channel(s); decrement Bj by the total size of MAC SDUs served to logical channel j above; if any resources remain, all the logical channels selected in clause 5.4.3.1.2 are served in a strict decreasing priority order (regardless of the value of Bj) until either the data for that logical channel or the UL grant is exhausted, whichever comes first. Logical channels with equal applied priority should be served equally. Note: the value of Bj can be negative.' The MAC entity shall not transmit only padding BSR when data is available.
rows.causal_mechanism: TS 38.321 §5.4.3.1.3 defines the token-bucket resource allocation procedure where each logical channel j maintains a token variable Bj incremented by PBR x T each TTI. A resource allocation bug corrupts this procedure through: (1) misconfigured PBR values causing Bj to grow unboundedly for low-priority channels, starving high-priority bearers; (2) incorrect priority ordering violating the strict decreasing priority rule; (3) Bj state corruption causing misallocation across logical channel groups. All three modes produce irregular PRBs_DL_Current and UL_NPRB values with secondary UL_SNR degradation from suboptimal power distribution across misallocated resource blocks.
rows.oran_component_rationale: The MAC scheduler is in the O-DU, making it the primary component where the bug manifests. Near-RT RIC xApps influence resource allocation policies through the E2 interface, and a bug in xApp logic can propagate incorrect scheduling decisions to the O-DU.
rows.oran_spec_reference: O-RAN.WG6.O2 (O2 interface, O-DU management); O-RAN.WG3.E2 (E2 interface — Near-RT RIC resource management xApp)
rows.kg_evidence_summary: KG contains RRM (radio resource management), PRB utilization measurements, periodicBSR-Timer, retxBSR-Timer, MAC-CellGroupConfig, and resource allocation concepts. Near-RT RIC evidence present with E2 control for resource/scheduling.
rows.notes:
CONFIRMED. Reference upgraded from §5 (parent clause, too broad) to §5.4.3.1.3 (Allocation of resources — specific subclause). §5.3.1 (DL Assignment reception) evaluated and excluded: it governs HARQ process ID derivation and NDI toggling for downlink grant reception, not UL resource allocation logic. §5.4.3.1.3 is the precise governing clause: defines the Bj token-bucket allocation algorithm and strict priority ordering that a resource allocation bug would violate. Support class: Mechanism-level — 3GPP does not define 'resource allocation bug' as a fault label; §5.4.3.1.3 specifies the correct behavior that the bug violates.
Legacy validation/evidence note: Primary clause text confirmed from TS 38.321 §5.4.3.1.3. §5.3.1 (DL Assignment reception) evaluated and excluded — governs HARQ/NDI processing for received DL grants, not resource allocation across logical channels.

rows.onset_pattern: Real over-the-air anomaly; the dataset describes the jammer as alternating between active and idle periods.
rows.causal_mechanism: Real over-the-air jamming is present in TelecomTS. The dataset describes interference on frequencies used by mobile devices, causing packet loss and anomalous network behavior.
